title: Fermented Cassava Flatbread with Sun-Dried Tomato Spread
summary: Highlighting South America's rich culinary traditions, this unique Brazilian flatbread showcases the incredible tangy flavor of a fermented component. Naturally fermented cassava pulp is mixed with tapioca starch, coconut oil, and crushed sea salt to create a pliable, elastic dough. Griddled on a blistering hot cast-iron skillet, these flatbreads puff beautifully, creating a delightfully crisp exterior wrapper around a chewy, airy interior structure. A vibrant spread made from sun-dried tomatoes, toasted pumpkin seeds, garlic, and cold-pressed olive oil adds a savory, umami-rich layer of flavor. Fresh cilantro, sliced red onion, and creamy goat cheese crumble complete this satisfying plant-forward creation. Ideal for light lunches or party appetizers, this recipe turns humble cassava root into a sophisticated bread alternative naturally free of gluten. Packed with healthy fats, gut-friendly fermented notes, and essential trace minerals, this flatbread offers a memorable tasting experience that will impress any bread lover.

steps.step: Measure out two cups of active fermented cassava starter paste into a large mixing bowl.
Check fermented starter for pleasant sharp tangy aroma before proceeding with dough.
Add tapioca starch, chia seeds, flaxseeds, cumin seeds, and fine sea salt into starter.
Pour in three tablespoons of warm melted coconut oil to add richness and texture.
Add xanthan gum, baking powder, and a pinch of turmeric powder to boost dough elasticity.
Stir ingredients together using a sturdy wooden spoon until a shaggy dough begins forming.
Pour in warm water two tablespoons at a time while mixing to bring dough together.
Turn shaggy cassava dough out onto a clean work surface lightly dusted with cassava flour.
Knead dough smoothly for five minutes until supple, non-sticky, and completely cohesive.
Shape kneaded fermented dough into a neat ball and return to bowl under damp towel.
Let dough rest undisturbed at room temperature for thirty minutes to hydrate fully.
Clean work surface and prepare parchment paper sheets for rolling out flatbread rounds.
Divide rested dough into six equal portion balls, rolling each smoothly between palms.
Keep dough balls covered under damp kitchen towel so they do not dry while waiting.
Place sun-dried tomatoes with their oil, toasted pumpkin seeds, and garlic into food processor.
Add extra virgin olive oil, lime juice, apple cider vinegar, and honey into processor bowl.
Add smoked paprika, chili powder, oregano, thyme, salt, and pepper into tomato mix.
Pulse food processor ten times to chop ingredients before blending into coarse paste.
Process spread mixture for two minutes until thick, vibrant red, and spreadably smooth.
Transfer sun-dried tomato spread into small bowl and taste for salt and lime balance.
Stir in chopped fresh jalapeno and lemon zest for extra kick and bright herbal lift.
Cover tomato spread container and store at room temperature while cooking flatbreads.
Clean food processor bowl immediately to prevent tomato oils from staining plastic.
Slice red onion paper-thin on a mandoline slicer and toss with lime juice in bowl.
Slice ripe avocado thinly and fan out slices on a plate, drizzling with olive oil.
Crumble fresh goat cheese into small nuggets and keep chilled in refrigerator until needed.
Wash fresh arugula leaves thoroughly and dry them completely in salad spinner basket.
Set out sesame seeds, sunflower seeds, and sea salt flakes in small topping bowls.
Place one dough ball between two sheets of unbleached parchment paper on work counter.
Press down dough ball with palm of hand to flatten into thick disk shape initially.
Roll out dough evenly using wooden rolling pin until disk reaches eight inches diameter.
Peel top layer of parchment paper off rolled flatbread round gently and carefully.
Dust rolled flatbread top lightly with extra tapioca starch to prevent sticking later.
Repeat rolling process for remaining five dough balls between parchment paper sheets.
Stack rolled flatbread rounds with parchment sheets between them to prevent sticking.
Inspect rolled dough rounds for uniform eighth-inch thickness to ensure even griddling.
Sprinkle sesame seeds and sunflower seeds onto one side of each dough round, pressing in.
Trim any ragged dough edges using round pastry cutter if perfectly neat circles desired.
Keep stacked flatbread rounds covered with damp cloth while preheating cast-iron skillet.
Prepare wide spatula near stove to turn hot flatbreads smoothly during cooking step.
Set baking sheet lined with clean towel inside warm 200 degree oven for cooked bread.
Place heavy cast-iron skillet or griddle pan over medium-high heat on stove burner.
Brush skillet surface lightly with avocado oil using silicone pastry brush to coat.
Carefully transfer first flatbread round onto hot dry skillet surface seed-side down.
Cook flatbread for two minutes until bottom turns golden with characteristic brown spots.
Watch for dough surface to bubble and puff up as steam expands inside structure.
Flip flatbread over using wide spatula and cook second side for ninety seconds more.
Press down edges gently with spatula to ensure even contact with hot skillet surface.
Transfer cooked flatbread to warm towel-lined baking sheet in oven to keep soft.
Repeat griddling process for remaining five flatbreads, re-oiling pan lightly as needed.
Adjust stove burner heat slightly if skillet becomes too smoking hot between batches.
Ensure each flatbread is fully cooked through with appealing crisp spots on both sides.
Keep all cooked griddled flatbreads wrapped in warm cloth until ready to assemble toppings.
Turn off stove burner safely once final flatbread is removed from hot skillet surface.
Lay warm cooked fermented cassava flatbreads out onto clean wooden serving boards.
Spoon two generous tablespoons of sun-dried tomato spread onto center of each bread.
Spread tomato mixture evenly across top of each flatbread, leaving half-inch border free.
Arrange sliced avocado fan pieces artfully over sun-dried tomato spread on each flatbread.
Scatter crumbled fresh goat cheese nuggets evenly over avocado and tomato layer.
Top flatbreads with pickled red onion slices, sliced black olives, and fresh arugula.
Scatter fresh cilantro leaves and chopped parsley over assembled toppings for green color.
Drizzle extra virgin olive oil and rich balsamic glaze lightly across all toppings.
Finish each flatbread with light sprinkling of sea salt flakes and cracked black pepper.
Scatter grated parmesan cheese over tops for extra savory umami punch if desired.
Inspect assembled flatbreads to verify balanced colorful presentation across all six portions.
Slice flatbreads into quarters using sharp pizza cutter wheel before carrying to table.
Serve immediately while flatbreads remain warm and crisp around golden griddled edges.
Present sliced cassava flatbread boards family style at center of table for sharing.
Pair flatbreads with fresh tropical fruit juices or cold iced teas for refreshing meal.
Provide extra sun-dried tomato spread in small side dip bowl with spoon for guests.
Offer additional lime wedges at table for guests to squeeze over fresh salad toppings.
Enjoy unique tangy flavor and crispy chewy texture of fermented cassava bread dough.
Highlight natural gluten-free whole food benefits of cassava starter dough to guests.
Wipe wooden serving boards clean after meal using warm soapy cloth and dry immediately.
Store leftover flatbreads wrapped tightly in foil in refrigerator for up to three days.
Reheat leftover flatbreads in dry skillet for one minute per side to restore crunch.
Store remaining tomato spread in glass jar in fridge for up to one week use.
Use remaining spread as condiment for sandwiches, grain bowls, or grilled vegetables.
Celebrate rich traditional South American cassava fermentation methods in home kitchen.
Conclude meal with light berry dessert to complement warm savory cassava flatbreads.
